out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Access to Handwashing Sink
violations.observation: The handwashing facility located at the end of the cookline is blocked (multiple metal pots in the sink basin), preventing access by employees for easy handwashing.
violations.corrective_action: A hand washing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use. CDI: CFM removed metal pots from hand sink basin.

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at the handwashing sink at the end of the cookline (the only hand sink in the back kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. CDI: CFM placed hand soap at the hand sink.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: container of cracked raw shelled eggs stored above RTE cooked chow mein noodles inside the Natural 3 Dr flattop refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CDI: CFM relocated container of cracked raw shelled eggs to bottom shelf inside the flattop refrigerator. CHILI WOK (Inspection Date: 05/04/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: uncooked chicken breast stored above uncooked shrimp and fish inside the walk in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). CDI: CFM relocated uncooked fish and shrimp to top shelf inside the walk in refrigerator.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: multiple TCS food items left out on prep counters and shelves at room temperature (not TPHC): commercially prepared breaded tempura chicken bites 49F, shredded cabbage 45F, steamed broccoli 48F, raw shelled eggs 47F, and raw bean sprouts 46F.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CDI: CFM placed shredded cabbage and bean sprouts in ice bath and commerically prepared breaded tempura chicken bites and steamed brocolli were relocated to 3 Dr Dukers flattop refrigerator until needed. CFM relocated raw shelled eggs to walk in refrigerator. EHS advised to utilize ice baths or TPHC if TCS food items are not under temperature control and maintaining temperature of 41F or below.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: two unlabeled bulk rice containers.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS instructed CFM to label bulk rice containers.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.title: Openings Protected from Pest Entry
violations.observation: Openings to the exterior of the building are present along the base (gap) of the back door in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Fill or close holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings to protect against the entry of insects and rodents. EHS instructed CFM to repair to gap at the base of the back door in the kitchen area to prevent rodent/ insect entrance.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: Observed the food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. CDI: EHS emailed CFM copy of written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.

out_items.name: No bare hand contact with ready-to-eat food, or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed

violations.title: No Bare Hand Contact with RTE Foods
violations.observation: Food employee(s) was observed handling the following ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands: food employee observed picking up hydrated noodles off table with barehands and putting back in bag.
violations.corrective_action: Except when washing fruits and vegetables, food employees may not contact ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands. Employees shall be using suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, or clean disposable gloves to handle all ready-to-eat foods. Proper handling of food and effective handwashing procedures will help prevent foodborne illness. CDI: CFM discarded bag or hydrated noodles.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: uncooked chicken stored above RTE cauliflower inside walk in refrigerator, uncooked kidney stored above RTE broccoli inside walk in refrigerator, uncooked beef stored above uncooked tofu inside walk in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CDI: CFM relocated uncooked chicken, kidney, and beef to bottom shelf inside the walk in refrigerator.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: observed recently prepped/ chopped chicken (51F) stored in the top of Atosa 3 Dr preptop refrigerator without properly cooling to 41F before cold holding.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. CDI: CFM relocated chicken to walk in refrigerator until internal temperature is 41F or below before placing in cold holding unit.

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.title: Thermometers, Location in Holding Units
violations.observation: Observed ambient (air/water) temperature measuring device missing from several cold hold units ( Atosa 3 Dr preptop refrigerator, Duker 3Dr under-counter refrigerator, and 2 Dr under-counter refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: In a mechanically hot food storage unit, the sensor of a temperature measuring device shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the coolest part of the hot food storage unit. Store the thermometer near the opening of the unit. EHS instructed CFM to place ambient thermometer in the warmest part of all cold hold units.

violations.observation: Observed gap under and along the side of the back door in the kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Fill or close holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings to protect against the entry of insects and rodents. CDI: EHS instructed CFM to repair gap under and along side of the back door in kitchen area.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Observed multiple bowls of food sitting on the floor (less than 6 inches) throughout the kitchen area.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. CDI: CFM instructed food staff keep food off the floor and prep food using counter.

out_items.name: Plumbing installed, proper backflow devices

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Air Gap Provided
violations.observation: Observed a hose attached to a faucet fixture. The hose extended below the flood rim level of the sink basin. Observed an air gap between the water supply outlet of 3 vat sink basin and sprayer (hanging into sink basin due to loose spring) is not observed.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by providing an air gap as specified under 5-202.13. CDI: CFM scheduled maintenance to repair sprayer spring during inspection.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' CFM could not provide or describe components of an employee health policy.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703-246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435. EHS provided written employee health policy for all employees to review and sign.

violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. CFM instructed staff to put on hats.
